newsitem.title: INDIA: Security man, 7 separatists die in India gunbattle.
newsitem.headline: Security man, 7 separatists die in India gunbattle.

text.p: Seven Naga tribal separatists and one Indian security man were killed in a gunbattle on Saturday in the remote northeastern state of Nagaland, police said.
The gunbattle broke out when Indian security forces raided guerrilla hideouts at Jotsoma near the state capital of Kohima, they said.

Police and paramilitary troops started intensive patrolling in the wooded, hilly terrain of the state near the Burmese border this week after Naga guerrillas massacred 30 bus passengers from the rival Kuki tribe on Monday.

More than 1,000 people have been killed in violence that began in mid-1992, when Nagas and Kukis began fighting for control of a strategic highway, which authorities say they use to transport drugs from Burma's golden triangle to Europe.

The Naga guerrillas, who follow a vaguely Maoist ideology, see the Kukis as pro-India. Violence between the two tribes has been centred in the neighbouring state of Manipur, where Kukis and Nagas live side by side.
